text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
* Tension has resurfaced within the ruling Socialist Party over constitutional reform.

* A recent agreement between the state and the Sonae retail group to buy tourism company Torralta may be at risk because casino operators are objecting to the conditions the government granted for the future running of the Torralta casino.
* Credits set up to help farmers get out of debt have been available for a month and only 15 farmers have applied because of insufficient publicity.

* The president of Chrysler Europe, Timothy Adams, told the paper that the company was studying ways of building up its presence in Portugal and might be interested in setting up a components factory.
* The government is looking at ways of offering early retirement from the age of 55, an official source told the paper.
* The government will increase its tax on diesel by two escudos, taking advantage of a fall in prices.
* A survey conducted by the Portuguese Industrial Association concluded that 86 percent of Portuguese companies have their tax situation in order.
* A police investigation has found that economic crime is widespread in Portugal. The biggest problem is the increase in of the number of off-shore businesses which escape proper regulation.
